_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 11 Geography P1 (Climate and Weather, Geomorphology and Geographical Skills and Techniques), November 2025 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper1.pdf, paper1_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Figures, maps,
graphs and photographs are described in [FIGURE: ...] brackets inside 'context'. memo_answer is
from the official marking guideline (English); mark allocations such as (2) are kept, one
accepted point per line. Column A/B items use the Grade 12 '[Y ... / Z ...]' style.
FORMAT: Section A Question 1 The Atmosphere (60) and Question 2 Geomorphology (60); Section B
Question 3 Geographical Skills and Techniques (30) on the 1:50 000 topographic map (extract from
2930 AC and AD HOWICK) and the 1:10 000 orthophoto map (2930AC 25 HOWICK). All three questions are
compulsory (150). The combined map sheet ships as a separate PDF inside the question-paper zip
(paper_download_url); it is not tracked here because of its size (about 37 MB), so map-read
inputs come from the memo's accepted values. Sub-parts (a)/(b) are kept in one entry.
The general information gives Howick's co-ordinates as 20º28' S as printed (Howick lies at about

questions.context: 1.5 Read the extract below on the effects of drought and desertification in Harry Gwala District Municipality. DROUGHT AND DESERTIFICATION: Drought and desertification in the Harry Gwala District Municipality, KwaZulu-Natal, impact communities through reduced water availability, diminished crop production and loss of agricultural land. This is leading to food insecurity and potential migration to urban areas. These events also cause increased run-away fires, high erosion and loss of species and habitat.
questions.text: What is desertification?
questions.topic: Climate and Weather: Droughts and desertification
questions.memo_answer: The process where once fertile soil becomes arid

questions.text: Quote, from the extract, environmental impacts caused by the events of drought and desertification.
questions.topic: Climate and Weather: Droughts and desertification
questions.memo_answer:
Loss of agricultural land (1)
Increased runaway fires (1)
High erosion (1)
Loss of habitat (1)
Reduced water availability (1)
[ANY THREE]

questions.text: Outline the natural causes of desertification.
questions.topic: Climate and Weather: Droughts and desertification
questions.memo_answer:
Climate change ‒ global warming and shifts in weather patterns can worsen desertification (2)
Prolonged periods without rain reduces vegetation and soil moisture, leaving the soil vulnerable (2)
High erosion (2)
Loss of top soil leads to soil degradation (2)
Uncontrolled fires can destroy vegetation leading to increase soil erosion (2)
Increased erosion (2)
[ANY TWO]

questions.text: Recommend THREE management strategies to reduce desertification.
questions.topic: Climate and Weather: Droughts and desertification
questions.memo_answer:
Practise land management (2)
Reforestation of the area (2)
Enhance soil fertility (2)
Reduce the size of cattle herds to work within the land carrying capacity (2)
Explore other income generating activities that have less impact on the environment (2)
[ANY THREE]
